Buffalo Bills/NFL Offseason Thread: Training Camp starts July 29
A Few Offseason Thoughts - Definitely in no particular order
stories.summary:
This might be more for me than any of you, as I feel like this might be the most checked out I've been in a Bills offseason.  I know I needed a break after the Denver loss because to me, out of all our playoff losses, I really felt like we were the better team and it started to feel like this team just can't get out of their own way.  Seeing Josh so distraught hit me in the feels, and the firing of McD left me very torn.  I found it tough to process anything about football for a while and I really didn't pay attention to much NFL talk until FA and the Draft.  Going to Buffalo last weekend for the "scrimmage" got my mind going and I've been binging podcasts for the past few weeks.  With that being said, consider this me shaking off the rust....



	 



	1 - Podcasts - I typically stream by Bills content via WGR through the Audacy app, but I've found their Bills coverage to be lacking recently.  I don't know if it's more to do with the Sabres being relevant again or if they are unhappy the Bills are trying to direct people to their own site, but it's just not the same to me.  I recently discovered the Buffalo Plus and SHOUT! and would recommend them to anyone on here.  Buffalo Plus updates about twice a week, recently added Micah Hyde as a weekly co-host, and I find them talking about a lot of the topics that I find interesting. They have a good rapport and keep it under 45 minutes usually.  SHOUT! is almost every other day, covered every day of training camp, and is a bit more analytical.  One of the hosts can be a bit hard to hear at times, but it's still pretty good content.



	 



	2 - The Stadium Transfer - I'm hesitant to talk about this so early, so please give me some grace.  Everything I'm about to say is just my own speculative curiosity.  Let me get this out of the way first.  I didn't love the new stadium.  However, as I pulled up to area and saw the old stadium in a pile of rubble, it hit me harder than I expected.  All the memories and nostalgia just hit me all at once.  I think in comparison to that, I wasn't going to like any new stadium and just wanted the Ralph back.  The new stadium felt like I was at an away game and overall felt sterile.  While they did a lot of things to represent the Bills in the concourses, it still felt impersonal to me.  Maybe it's because it was painted all black, who knows?  It was frustrating to have the escalators not working when we needed them and certain food vendors to not be fully stocked.  I walked the entire stadium and every section.  The upper decks are no joke.  Those steps are super steep and for someone who doesn't like heights, I'm glad my seats aren't up there.  But there's no denying that every seat is much closer to the field, albeit higher up.  One thing that really annoyed me was the lack of televisions around the concourse.  In the old stadium, I could walk around the concourse and never miss a moment of the game because I could always see a TV.  Now, they have larger flat screens more spread out.  When it rained, people were scrambling to find a TV to watch on, but I actually got told multiple times that we weren't allowed to stand and block the area.  That's a miss to me.  Last complaint was the sound system and scoreboard.  While the sound system was louder, it got worse as the game went on.  The bass was terrible and I couldn't make out what they were saying in the post-game sideline interviews.  I'm hoping these are settings they can tweak.  The scoreboards are fine, but they do not reflect a new stadium to me.  I don't want anything crazy like at Citi-Field or in New England, but I think it's bizarre they are smaller than the old stadium.  Oh yeah, seeing people having to run to the concourses due to weather in the very first fan event was beautifully ironic.



	 



	Now, with that being said, the memories and familiarity will come.  They will make tweaks as the preseason goes one and I'm sure people will learn to love it.  I overall find the entire discussion about the stadium to be fascinating.  There seems to be the complainers (throw me in there) and the grateful.  To me, the Bills brought this on themselves when they set the PSL prices, ticket prices, and talked about there not being a bad seat in the house.  I understand that the new stadium is a more accurate reflection of pricing in the current NFL.  However, our fans aren't used to that.  So when you ask for huge PSL deposits, ticket prices jumping up 30% or more, and are now the hottest ticket in town, you have to accept that people are going to be more critical because they paid for the right to be.  I think everyone wants to love the new stadium, besides the internet trolls, because I know I did.  I'm hoping my opinions will change at the opener, but those are my thoughts.



	 



	3 - Texans Opener - When I first saw the schedule, I wasn't thrilled that we were opening in Houston.  As time went on, I think that is the absolute best possible opener we could have.  After the Denver loss, you could see it on the players faces that something needed to change because they were starting to believe they couldn't get it done.  A belief that you will find a way to win or lose is just as important as what you do on the field.  Pegula handled the major shake-up part by firing McD, which I think will bring a natural change.  The next step is to get another monkey off our back.  Josh has not had good success in Houston by any means.  If we can go in and handle business, I think that kind of win will go a long way in changing the player mentality that things might finally start being different.  



	 



	4 - Base Defense - I'm still learning about the 3-4 defense and how we will implement it but let me just say that I've never been more excited to watch a pre-season game and watch a vanilla defense.  At the scrimmage, I saw 5 guys on the line who should all command single blocks.  Chubb, Sanders, Walker, Oliver, Groot.  Without any exotic blitzes or coverages, I cannot wait to see what those guys do to opposing offensive lines.  If they can't get it done as is, then we have much bigger problems on our hands.  



	 



	5 - Beane - Leonard had a quote in an interview a few months back where he discussed not having all the pieces he wanted on defense and it will probably take a year or two to get there.  When I think about the recent draft and us drafting back-ups with our first two picks, it makes me wonder why that was the priority over pieces that Leonard needs for his defense.  I don't disagree that we needed DB depth and another pass rusher, but with our first two picks?  Granted, I don't know what the Bills board looked like and if there was even anyone available that Leonard would consider a starter for his scheme, but I would think there were better options.  Also, I can't say that I've heard a great report about Davison Igbinosun so far in training camp so I hope we get value for that pick at some point.  I still think Beane does a great job with contracts and can evaluate talent in certain spots, but if this defensive line doesn't produce after all the money and draft capital we put into it or the receivers fail to produce again, then I really hope he's on a short leash.  



	 



	6 - Scrimmage Thoughts - I hesitate to call what I witnessed on Saturday a scrimmage as they maybe did 11 on 11 for 20 minutes total.  It is frustrating that Brady course corrected this to be a practice when even the tickets said it would be a scrimmage.   Either way, from what I did see, Palmer did not have a great day and I don't feel like any of the receivers outside of Moore, Shakir, and Kincaid did themselves any favors.  One thing that became abundantly clear is that we will be throwing the to RB's a lot more, in both actual RB screens and wheel routes.  I think this will be great new option for Josh.  Additionally, we seem to be practicing the deep ball more and Shakir is part of that.  I think we are going to see a different offense that prioritizes stretching the field and getting everyone involved.  As for the defense, I do think some of those deep balls would have been sacks if the defenders didn't have to pull up short of Josh.  Benford seemed to get worked by Moore quite a few times and Chubb is absolutely massive. I don't think I realized how big that guy is.  He also was great after the practice by walking around the stadium and signing mini-foam footballs for the fans.



	 



	7 - WR 4 - With all this talk about who will be WR 3 and 4, I feel pretty confident in saying that they won't be receivers.  Moore and Shakir are 1 and 2.  3 and 4, to me, is going to be a combination of Kincaid or Cook.  From everything I've seen, this seems to be the focus of the offense and they will allow Palmer, Coleman (so sick of talking about him btw), and Bell to compete for the remaining targets. 



	 



	8 - Elarms-Orr - I want to keep my expectations in check, but man do I think Elarms-Orr is going to be a monster for us.  He covered Cook at full speed on a seam route.  He is incredibly fast to the ball and wants to hurt people.  I see a personal foul in his immediate future if not an arrest warrant for homicide.  Nothing against Bernard and Williams, but I want to see KEO out there so I can get his jersey.



	 



	9 - Grace for new coaches - While we had rookie HC's in Seattle and Jacksonville show immediate success last season, and the Bills are in their Championship window, I do think there needs to be some grace for the new coaches.  With Brady, I expect him to lose us at least one game due to rookie coach decisions, whether it be poor clock management, a bad challenge, or something basic.  For Brady, I just want to see the players show up for every game (No Miami letdowns) and I want to see some easy throws on 3rd and 4th down for Josh, where he doesn't have to put on his cape and figure it out.  I have more grace for Leonard, because it's an entirely new system with a lot of new players on the team.  Also, as we've seen with aggressive 3-4 defenses, the big plays go both ways.  While I expect to see sacks and turnovers go up, I also expect to see us give up more big plays.



	 



	10 - Josh - First off, congrats on the daughter.  It's been so great to see Josh talk about being a dad, how his priorities have shifted, and his overall apparent refreshed status.  You can tell the Denver game is in the past.  His deep ball looks great.  His energy seems great.  I think he's in for a monster season.  I also appreciate the way he's been handling all the media criticism about the stadium, uniforms (bleh), and Bills lack of success. We need Josh to be at the top of his game because this schedule is no joke and we have competition in the East. I see at least 4k yards this season, a little less running, and less turnovers this season.  I expect Josh to hit the ground running, handle the Texans, and have a different level of swagger this season. 



	 



	 



	I may have rambled a bit, but it's good to get writing again.  For those of you who hung in there the whole post, I appreciate you.  I can honestly say I'm looking forward to writing game recaps again as there is so many new things to pay attention to.  The last few years felt like the same recap over and over again.  So here's to something new.

On Game Days, Would You Attend a Pre-Game Happy Hour in the Stadium with Discounted Food & Drinks?
stories.summary:
Inspired by all the recent new-stadium talk, I had an idea for the Bills to offer fans a good non-tailgating pregame option.



	 



	If, for a 1 PM kickoff, the gates opened at 11 AM and all food and drinks were offered at significantly reduced prices (think Atlanta’s “Fan First” pricing) until 12:30 PM, effectively creating a 90-minute pregame “happy hour,” would you take advantage of it? And, hell, give season-ticket holders an extra 30 minutes until 1 PM (Utilize an app with a QR code or something).



	 



	I love a good tailgate, but the atmosphere isn't always family-friendly, and it can also be a bit cumbersome having to prepare and bring everything you need. Some people may also simply want to get to the new stadium well before the game starts and check it out. I think offering a 90-minute window with reasonably priced food and drinks would give fans a legitimate alternative to tailgating. It would still give tailgaters plenty of flexibility, too. You could tailgate from 9–11:30, head into the stadium, check things out, top off your drink, and grab a cheap snack before kickoff.



	What I really like about this idea is that it makes sense from all sides.



	 



	From the Bills’ perspective: They probably don't sell a ton of food and drinks between 11 AM and 12:30 PM anyway. And because fans aren't a truly “captive” audience yet, you can't simply charge stadium prices and expect everyone to pay when they have the option of eating and drinking in the parking lot. Ending the discounted pricing 30+ minutes before kickoff also allows the Bills to transition back to normal stadium pricing when fans become more of a captive audience.



	 



	On top of that, it would be a nice goodwill gesture toward fans. It could generate some positive PR, likely at little to no additional cost, while also improving the overall fan experience by getting more people into the stadium earlier and reducing the rush that typically happens in the 30–45 minutes before kickoff.



	 



	From the fans’ perspective:  This takes nothing away from anyone. Prefer to tailgate? Go for it. You can still enter the stadium whenever you want. Don't want to deal with the hassle of tailgating, or want a more family-friendly option? You can arrive when the gates open, get reasonably priced food and drinks, and spend some time checking out everything the new stadium has to offer.



	 



	If the Bills offered something like this, would you take advantage of it?

What are your expectations for the defense this coming season?
stories.summary:
The Bills are so young on defense.  Projected starters Sanders, Hairston and Walker are all second year players, Williams (assuming he beats out Orr (r)) will be a 1st year full time starter in his 4th season.  Bishop is in his 3rd season.  Now add how much of the key depth are projected to be rookies in Orr, Pride, Parker, Kilgore, and Igbinosun. Other depth is raw in Hancock (2nd year), Andressen (3rd) and Carter (3rd, but lost 1 year plus to injuries).  
	 



	There are good to excellent vets like Groot, Chubb, Benford, Oliver and Bernard (if he can adjust to the new system and stay healthy), but there are also new vets with big question marks like Stone, Alford and Gardner-Johnson (already injured). 
	 



	Put this all together and what do you got….. ?  Honestly I have no idea.  
	 



	My heart tells me that if they stay healthy they will improve steadily throughout the season as the kids get used to the speed of the NFL and all the players get used to playing in the new scheme with a new defensive coaching staff.  My head tells me that there are going to be huge bumps in the road and Josh and the offense will have to win some shootouts to keep us in contention.

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #23 Gavin McCarthy
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Gavin McCarthy



Drafted: 2023, BUF (86th overall), 3rd round, 22nd pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born:  6/2/2005 (Age: 21) Troy, New York (grew up in Clarence Center)



2025-2026 stats: GP 36 G 4 A 17 PTS 21, Boston University



2025 T25U25 Ranking:  Unranked



Here we go again with another young right-shot defenseman in the organization. This one is a local kid from Clarence Center and a former Buffalo Jr. Sabre, making his path to the team a little more interesting for Sabres fans.



Gavin McCarthy is a solid 21-year-old defender coming off three seasons at Boston University. Each year, he took another step offensively, steadily increasing his production. In 2025-26, he finished with four goals and 21 points in 36 games while serving as captain of the Terriers.



McCarthy is a physical, two-way defenseman who isn’t afraid to lay a big hit and make his presence felt. He has decent size at 6’2″ and 196 pounds. While his offensive skills are certainly respectable, his two-way label leaned more toward the defensive side of the game in college. He projects as the type of D-man who can be trusted to play a sound, physical game in his own end while providing some secondary offense when the opportunity presents itself.



His skating is strong and one of his best traits. It allows him to take risks and still get back into the play.







Gavin signed a three-year entry-level contract with the Sabres on March 17th. McCarthy will continue his development with the Rochester Americans, turning pro for his first full AHL season. He did get a brief taste of the pro game last year, appearing in five games with the Amerks late in the campaign.



The Sabres will keep watch on this quality player and see if he can eventually find a place in Buffalo a few years down the road. We all know just how crowded the field is when it comes to defensive prospects in the organization, with talented young blueliners up the wazoo. For now, McCarthy should be a strong addition to Rochester, bringing his physicality and leadership qualities to the Amerks. Only time will tell if he can take the next step and prove he is truly NHL material.

Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #24: Topias Leinonen
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Topias Leinonen



Drafted: 2022 – 2nd Round (41st Overall)



Position: Goalie



Born: January 25th, 2004 – 22 Years Old



2025-2026 stats: AHL – 3-3-0, 3.48 GAA, .855 SV%. ECHL: 3-1-1, 3.24 GAA, .880 SV%.



2025 T25U25 Ranking: 24



Topias Leinonen was looking to build on a solid development year in 2024-2025 and use that momentum to spur the beginning of his North American career. With a crowded crease in Rochester, it was a struggle for him to find playing time in the AHL. A lower body injury sidelined him in early December that kept him out through January. He was assigned to the Jacksonville Icemen in February where he appeared in 5 games.



The 2024-2025 season is starting to look like the outlier when it comes to Leinonen’s health. He’s struggled to stay healthy in nearly every season since being the first goalie drafted in 2022. The lack of ice time has severely limited his career development. This lack of growth is reflected in our rankings as he once again takes the 24th spot.



If, and that’s a massive “if”, he can stay healthy, Leinonen should have the opportunity for more consistent ice time this year. There is one less goalie prospect in the organization after the trade of Devon Levi. Hopefully Leinonen can seize the opportunity and put a full season of on ice development on his resume.

stories.title: Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25: #25 Simon-Pier Brunet
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Simon-Pier Brunet



Drafted: 2024, BUF (123rd overall), 4th round, 26th pick



Position: Defense (shoots right)



Born: 10/24/2005 (Age: 20) Gatineau, Quebec, CAN



2025-2026 stats: GP 54 G 2 A 24 PTS 26, QMJHL Victoriaville Tigres



2025 T25U25 Ranking:  Unranked



A few late straggler votes were enough to nudge defenseman Simon-Pier Brunet into the Buffalo Sabres’ Top 25 Under 25 rankings. Unfortunately for 2026 sixth-round pick Dylan Dumont, that meant falling off the list and into the abyss—at least until next year.



Dumont still gets a mention here, though, mostly because I had already completed his profile before the late votes came in to change things. The tardy tallies caused a bit of a shuffle in the 21-25 range of the rankings, so here is the final updated version.



By the way DBTBers, there were only 92 votes for this!? We had 117 last summer. After the great season Buffalo just had, (and with many new members here now) I expected much more partcipation. I don’t speak for the whole staff here but I’m shaking my head at the low turn out, with a frowny-faced emoji thrown in too!



So, what should you know about Simon-Pier Brunet?



Let’s start with the basics. Brunet stands 6-foot-2, weighs 204 pounds, and is currently 20 years old. During the 2025-26 season, he recorded 26 points in 54 games with the Victoriaville Tigres of the QMJHL after being traded from the Drummondville Voltigeurs. (where he had posted 32 points in 60 games the previous year—the same club the Buffalo Sabres selected him from in the 2024 NHL Draft) His offensive production is respectable for a stay-at-home blueliner, but putting up points is not what defines his game.



Brunet’s best attributes are in his own zone, particularly his ability to guard the front of the net. You can’t go through him and he is difficult to get around. He can wall off the opposition from the high-danger areas with his brawn and determination. He is also a sound skater with a good motor to his game.







After playing two more seasons in the QMJHL after his draft year, Brunet has committed to Merrimack College for the 2026 -27 season. He will thankfully have time there to work on his game more. Buffalo has an abundance of young defensemen right now, especially those of the right shot variety. His pathway to the NHL will depend not only on his develpment but how the Sabres handle their other defensive prospects.



At this juncture, it almost feels like a few other young defenders will need to fail spectacularly or be traded elsewhere to open up a lane for Simon-Pier Brunet. Or he could forge his way onto the team eventually with his solid defense and physical style of play. It might take both for that to happen.



Meanwhile, he will be one to keep an eye on. Brunet is not a top defensive prospect in the Sabres’ deep system but he could be a top underdog.



2026 Buffalo Sabres Top 25 Under 25



#25 Simon-Pier Brunet

2026 Top 25 Under 25: Honorable Mentions
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Thanks to all 92 people who responded to Die By The Blade’s annual voting for the Buffalo Sabres’ Top 25 Under 25 list. Before we get into the list, let’s take a moment for the honorable mentions – aka, the players who didn’t make the top 25.



There were 42 eligible players this year. Several players on last year’s top 25 list aged out while others are no longer with the organization.



Let’s kick things off with a few players who just missed the cut for making the top 25. The scoring in the lower ranks is very close, and in some cases flawed too since a number of voters only ranked their top 10-20 players, and left the remainder of the names in the alphabetical order they were originally placed in. This means by default a Simon-Pier Brunet got more voting points than a Vasily Zelenov, whether or not one is better than the other. 



30. Scott Ratzlaff (G)



The goaltender will turn 21 in a month, and sees himself drop from 25th to 30th not because of waning performance, but more so the quality of prospects in the Sabres’ stable. Ratzlaff went 15GP, 3.10 GAA,  .913 sv% and a 5-7-2 record for the Jacksonville Icemen in the ECHL, and 13GP, 3.44 GAA,  .878 sv% and a 4-6-2 record for the Rochester Americans.  



29. Jake Richard (RW/LW)



The forward was drafted 170th overall by the Sabres in 2022, but after a breakthrough second season for Connecticut with 43 points and 16 PIM in 34 games, his performance dipped with 10G and 17A in 38 games, while racking up 42 PIM. He was in the honorable mentions last summer too. UConn lost to the Spartans (and their two Sabres, see below) in the first round of the playoffs, with Richard accumulating eight shots out of his team’s 42 in the 2-1 loss. 



28. Patrick Geary (D)



St. Francis grad Geary was drafted 172nd in 2024, and had a solid year at Michigan State University, where he wore the ‘A’ on his sweater. He had 2G and 9A in 35 games, with 70 PIM on the blue line leading MSU to the #3 seeding along with fellow Sabre blueliner prospect Maxim Strbak. Geary even scored in the regional final where they lost to Wisconsin, he’s definitely one to watch. 



27. Dylan Dumont (RW)



The 2026 188th pick is an intriguing prospect, scoring 28G and 16A in 62 games in the QMJHL. A scoring winger who attacks the center of the ice, Dumont was his team’s leading goal scorer last year. Drummondville coach Sylvain Favreau spoke in glowing terms of the youngster who turns 18 in a couple of weeks, saying he scored many of those goals off the rush and in front of the net by utilizing his best assets, his skating and soft hands. 



26. Zac Funk (LW/RW)



The Sabres acquired the forward in an ECHL trade this summer, sending Tyler Kopf to Washington for him. Funk, 22, scored 19 points (9+10) in 23 games last season with the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays. He also had two assists in 10 contests with Washington’s AHL affiliate, the Hershey Bears. The 6-foot-0, 210-pound winger has split his two professional campaigns between the ECHL and AHL after signing with Washington as an undrafted free agent at the end of the 2023-24 season, having led the WHL with 67 goals that year in 68 games for the Prince George Cougars.



Stay tuned as we break into the top 25 in a couple of days!

stories.title: Jedi Council
stories.summary:
Mad at Ads and Short on Grit Issue is Back



Hello fellow DBTBers, just a little Jedi Council to hopefully brighten your day. A new article for you to digest as we near the end of July, 2026 already. The poor kids here in Florida go back to school in just three weeks. I remember somewhere around September 7th for the start of the school year in Buffalo. I would have dreaded having to go back to school in the middle of August.



So away we go with a few topics of interest to me and hopefully you as well.



1. Casinos and Ironman Sponsorship?



As you may have heard, the Buffalo Sabres have joined most of the NHL by adding corporate advertising to their home and away jerseys. Color me disappointed to see our hometown team finally succumb to the almighty dollar. It wasn’t unexpected, but it’s still a little disheartening. I liked being one of the last hold outs on that commercialization nonsense. It was a point of pride that their sweaters remained untouched. Unfortunately, that’s no longer the case.



Former NHL Chief Operating Officer John Collins first brought the concept to the forefront in 2014, arguing that uniform sponsorships were inevitable. Unfortunately, he was right. Ads on NHL jerseys first originated as a league-wide initiative proposed by NHL executives and approved by the Board of Governors in August 2021 to generate massive new revenue streams.



Five years later, only two NHL teams (the Dallas Stars and the San Jose Sharks) do not have corporate jersey ad sponsors heading into the 2026-27 season. All other 30 teams have active jersey patch agreements. The Sabres will feature Seneca Resort and Casino on their home uniforms and Stark Tech on their road duds. Both will be small patches on the upper left side of the hockey jersey. That is Stark TECH by the way, not Stark Industries. No Avengers will be affiliated with the organization, sorry Marvel fans. 



Another company, Stark Naked, was turned down for obvious reasons.



Every NHL team now features an advertisement on their helmet, and most fans don’t seem to mind. Ads on jerseys, however, are a different story. To many hockey purists, they’re a blemish on the traditional beauty of a team’s sweater. I’m firmly in that camp as well.



With that in mind, here’s what the Sabres are presenting us with.







I know some people around here are not fond of the gambling industry that has really infiltrated the sports world in the last ten years. So the Seneca Resort and Casino sponsorship will never be appreciated by some. Visually speaking, at least the patch is also royal blue like the jersey and the lettering and logo are only white. There is thankfully no color mismatch between the two. A few NHL clubs out there sport colors on their ads in contrast to their team colors and it’s a real eyesore.



As far as the Stark Tech sponsorship on the road uniforms, the logo appears a little smaller than the Seneca home patch. The wording is a darker blue than the Sabres’ royal blue but barely noticeable from a distance. There is also some faint light blue and light green in the logo but the smaller size makes it hard to see. All in all, it could have been a lot worse. Neither patch is jarringly offensive, and eventually we will learn to live with them. I’m still going to bitch about it though, every chance I get. I absolutely loath the whole cash grab of having ads on hockey jerseys.



But if it’s going to be forced upon us, at least ours isn’t too obnoxious or embarrassing. No Chico’s Bail Bonds to be had.



2. True Grit



The Sabres have enough players who are willing to compete, but this offseason has left them with a shortage of players who consistently make opponents pay physically. The team dealt away size, strength and toughness in Jordan Greenway and Alex Tuch and also lost physical scrapper Josh Dunne to free agency. Buffalo added the monstrous Louis Crevier on the backend but no enhancement has been made to the forward ranks to replace that grit.









For years, Buffalo was viewed as a team that could be pushed around. Management recognized that and made a point of adding heavier, more abrasive players to the bottom of the lineup. They specifically targeted players who would forecheck, finish checks, and make the team harder to play against. Along with an occasional bout thrown in when needed. Last season’s Sabres were a team based on speed but they could throw their weight around too and answer the bell when needed. On paper, this year’s team may be even faster, but they don’t have as much muscle up front anymore. I worry that will cost them eventually, with the ‘roid rage goons of Tampa, always physical Boston and the newly hulked up Panthers just waiting to take cheap shots at them.



The 4th line of Krebs, Malenstyn and Carrick have tenacity and willingness to use the body on their opponents. All three will stick up for teammates but none of them are known for being a true protector on the ice. Beck is tough hombre’ but Krebs and Carrick don’t have the size to match their spirit. If the gloves come off, I say a quick prayer that neither player is going to get hurt and miss 20 games. Krebs in particular has a pattern of barely hanging on in his fights.



So where am I going with this? I believe the team is short at least one more physical forward. Somebody who forechecks hard, hits harder and is willing to throw down at a moment’s notice. A physical, go-to player the other team is always wary off. But the Sabres could also use a top-six forward to help replace Alex Tuch’s production too. Or at least a good portion of it. It’s highly doubtful they can bring in a 60-65 point player at this stage of the summer. But what about a 45 point one who also fills the grit and toughness aspect I’ve been going on about?



Enter the idea for Buffalo to aquire Utah’s Lawson Crouse. (yes, I’m still on this player for like 4 years now) The Sabres would be killing two birds with one stone trading for the big winger. He has all the traits I’ve been talking about that Buffalo is now short on. Crouse is a premier physical forward in the NHL, standing 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds. He is known for policing the ice and protecting his teammates, while dishing out heavy hits along the way. He can forecheck hard and obviously handle himself in a fight. He is the perfect addition for what the team lacks.



Crouse is not without skill or offensive ability, though, and that’s where the “two-for-one” value of acquiring him comes into play. Lawson has scored 20 or more goals in four of the past five seasons. Last year, he found the back of the net 24 times while adding 20 assists for 44 points, all while posting an NHL career-best +20 rating. He’s not the offensive dynamo that some of the fantasy trade proposals involving Buffalo have envisioned over the past several months. Realistically, Crouse is probably a middle-six forward on most NHL teams. That said, I believe the Sabres could utilize him very effectively on their second line. Surrounded by Buffalo’s high-end offensive talent, there’s even a chance his production could take another step forward.









Where Crouse really separates himself, however, is with the intangibles. He would instantly inject a much needed dose of size, toughness, and physicality into Buffalo’s top six while also serving as a protector for the team’s skilled players. Adding a forward who can contribute offensively while filling that role would address two major needs with one acquisition.



Lawson is also a regular and significant contributor on the penalty-killing unit, an area depleted by the departure of Alex Tuch. He frequently averages nearly three minutes of ice time per game while shorthanded. 



The 29 year old’s current contract pays him an expected annual salary (AAV) of $4.3 million. His multi-year deal is set to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, at which point he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent. His actual cap hit this year is only $3.9 million which the Sabres could easily finagle into the lineup. Any deal would likely involve Crouse signing an extension. I imagine he would be looking for something along the lines of $6-7 million per season and at least a five year deal which Buffalo could afford with extra cap space next year. He would be worth it in my opinion.



I feel most of us would like to add a goal scorer while also bringing in a banger to replace what we have lost. Crouse does that with one move from GMJK. I won’t speculate on what it would take to acquire him. Most trade ideas are shot down anyways as either too much or not enough to give up. If I’m the Sabres’ brass however, I’m considering what some goofy “writer” from this forum is pushing. Or even some intern named T. McGee. Buffalo has taken a hit this offseason both in toughness and offense. The young talent of Kulich, Ostlund and Helenius could certainly be a fill-in factor from within. But adding an experienced, physical forward and a proven goal scorer would add an extra layer of protection to the defending Atlantic Division Champions.



So will this actually come to fruition? Like most hopeful deals made by fans, probably not. Buffalo’s GM may be off parasailing right now or on his 5th cocktail in Aruba. But I feel that this move would address both problems the Sabres’ face amongst the forward ranks. To me, they are still short an experienced scoring forward and some overall heavy sandpaper. This would be a great option to fill both those needs.



If you made it this far, I hope everyone is enjoying their summer. The NHL regular season kicks off in only about 9 more weeks…
